recentItems.title: The Witcher 3 (Wine) - DX11, wine-staging 2.17, mesa 17.2, AMD Radeon 7870, Sep 2017
recentItems.description:
No ingame audio, because the audio recording was meh...

I heard the Witcher 3 works in Wine-staging so I tried it to see, if this is true and true it is. Maybe not the fastest, as you can see in the combat, it has some glitches and audio is distorted in cutscene videos (not ingame), but it works and looks gorgeous. Also a DX11 game, so quite the achievement.

Used wine-staging 2,17, mesa 17.2, Linux 4.12 (Arch Linux). Also radeon/radeonsi. No amdgpu.

Hardware: AMD Radeon 7870, Intel i5-4670, 8GB RAM.

recentItems.title: Linux Recording: SSR vs. OBS (GRID autosport)
recentItems.description:
Nowadays Linux gaming has two reasonable choices for recording videos. One is SSR and the other one is OBS. I used (after glc) SRR for a long time, but I heard OBS might be better (performancewise). Is it though? And are there drawbacks? This video tries to find that out. A little bit.

Please don't see it as a full benchmark test. I would have to test SSR and OBS more to get there. But if you have some tips or like to discuss my findings, please comment below. Thank you.

recentItems.description:
As of now (17.07.16) the game is out for Linux!

Reddit-Link:  https://www.reddit.com/r/linux_gaming/comments/3ywa22/howto_running_undertale_natively_on_linux/

recentItems.title: GRID Autosport Linux Performance AMD Radeon HD 7870 radeonsi driver
recentItems.description:
Please keep in mind, that software recording "costs" performance.

In this video I show you, how GRID Autosport performs on my pc with the radeonsi open-source driver on "ultra" settings (though seems to be not every effect is on ultra with the open-source driver).

About the launch option:
LANG=C LD_PRELOAD="../lib/x86_64/libtcmalloc_minimal.so:${LD_PRELOAD}" %command%

The "LANG=C" should be fixed with the next update. You need that, if you are in a "comma country". And I needed the other one or else it just crashes at the start of the race.

You need at least Mesa 11.0.2 compiled against LLVM 3.7 (not the case for Ubuntu 15.10! Unless you use ppa's).

My pc:
Intel i5-4670
AMD Radeon HD 7870
8GB RAM
Arch Linux 64bit

recentItems.title: Linuxgaming: Goodbye Catalyst, hello radeonsi
recentItems.description:
WIth Mesa 11 and DRI3 support, the radeonsi driver is sometimes slower, sometimes fast than the Catalyst driver and you could say overall on a par with it. Time for me to do the switch and say goodbye to Catalyst.

CPU: i5-4670
GPU: AMD Radeon HD 7870
8GB RAM
Arch Linux 64bit (testing + mesa-git repo)
Kernel 4.2
"KDE 5"/Plasma 5.4 with desktop effects disabled
Mesa git (Sep 2015, ~11.1)
radeonsi git (Sep 2015)
DRI3 enabled

In order to get Shadow of Morder working, you need (besides the git-versions of driver and such) the following launch option in Steam:

force_glsl_extensions_warn=true MESA_EXTENSION_OVERRIDE=GL_ARB_arrays_of_arrays %command%

Though some effects like rain are missing.
